newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's new Kurdish ally defies U.S. might.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's new Kurdish ally defies U.S. might.

text.p: Iraqi Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani, newly allied with President Saddam Hussein, on Tuesday echoed Baghdad's defiance of U.S. military might.

"I am not afraid of the cruise missiles," Barzani said in Kurdish through an interpreter, hours after U.S. missiles slammed into southern Iraqi targets in retaliation for weekend advances by Baghdad forces into the predominantly Kurdish north.

Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), told a press conference his faction had grown impatient with U.S. promises to nurture Kurdish autonomy in the north, behind a western air cover.
"It is for...years the Americans have played with us and have been onlookers," said Barzani of the KDP decision to throw in its lot with Saddam after years in the U.S. camp.
KDP guerrillas, backed by Iraqi regulars and armour, threw rival Kurds of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) out of the main northern city of Arbil on Saturday.
Dozens of U.S. cruise missiles struck military targets in southern Iraq earlier on Tuesday, in retaliation for Saddam's return to the north.
